# Workflow Management

The Workflow Management layer of docturnal handles the creation and management of the workflow file committed to each repository. This ensures that the workflow is up-to-date and configured correctly.

## Overview

The Workflow Management layer is responsible for generating and updating the `.github/workflows/docturnal.yml` file in each repository. This file defines the steps and settings for the GitHub Actions workflow that docturnal uses to add comments and update documentation.

## Responsibilities

- Generates the `.github/workflows/docturnal.yml` file.
- Manages the versioning of the workflow template.
- Checks if a workflow file uses the docturnal action.
- Determines the version of the workflow template used in a repository.

## Key components

| File | Purpose | Main definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`app/src/workflow.ts`](../app/src/workflow.ts) | Manages the workflow file committed to each repository. | `WORKFLOW_PATH`, `WORKFLOW_FILE`, `WORKFLOW_VERSION`, `workflowYaml`, `isOldTemplate`, `templateVersion` |

## How it works

The Workflow Management layer uses the `workflowYaml` function to generate the content of the `.github/workflows/docturnal.yml` file. This function includes the necessary steps and settings for the workflow, such as the comment level, existing code handling, and concurrency control.

The `workflowYaml` function takes the `actionRepository` as a parameter, which specifies the repository containing the docturnal action. It then constructs the YAML content for the workflow, including inputs for the comment level and existing code handling.

The layer also includes utility functions like `usesDocturnal`, `isOldTemplate`, and `templateVersion` to check if a workflow file uses the docturnal action, determine if it is an old template, and get the version of the workflow template used in a repository, respectively.

## Configuration

The Workflow Management layer does not require any configuration settings or environment variables. It reads the necessary information directly from the codebase and the GitHub Actions workflow file.
